readingSections.title: 1. Foundations - V, I, R, Power, KCL, KVL (From Zero)
readingSections.quickSummary: Current is charge flow, voltage is push, resistor obeys V=IR. KCL: currents at a node sum to zero. KVL: voltages around a loop sum to zero.
content: Charge $Q$ (coulombs), current $I = dQ/dt$ (amperes = coulombs/sec), voltage $V$ (joules/coulomb = push per charge), power $P = VI$ (watts). Passive sign convention: current enters the positive terminal of a load, so $P = VI$ absorbed is positive.

Ohm's law $V = IR$. Series: same current, resistances add $R_{eq} = R_{1}+R_{2}$. Parallel: same voltage, conductances add $1/R_{eq} = 1/R_{1}+1/R_{2}$ (two resistors: $R_{eq} = R_{1}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$). Voltage divider (series): $V_{1} = V_{s}R_{1}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$. Current divider (parallel): $I_{1} = I_{s}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$ (opposite arm on top).

KCL: algebraic sum of currents leaving a node = 0 (charge cannot pile up). KVL: algebraic sum of voltages around any closed loop = 0 (energyRound trip nets zero). Sign discipline: pick a traversal direction; voltage drop (+ to -) is negative rise... fix convention: sum of rises = sum of drops.
Worked example: $10V$ source, $R_{1}=2k$ series $R_{2}=3k$. Current $I = 10/5k = 2mA$. $V_{R2} = 2mA \times 3k = 6V$ (divider: $10 \times 3/5$). Power in $R_{2}$: $V^{2}/R = 36/3k = 12mW$.

subsections.title: Divider twins - which ratio?
content: Voltage divider: wanted resistor on TOP. Current divider: OPPOSITE resistor on top.
Mnemonic: voltage favours self, current favours the other branch.
Always verify: divider output must be smaller than source (passive).

subsections.title: KCL/KVL sign method that never fails
content: Label every resistor with + where assumed current enters. KCL at node: in = out. KVL loop: walking from + to - is a drop ($-IR$), - to + is a rise ($+IR$); sources $+V$ rising.
If a computed current is negative, direction was backwards - magnitude still right.

subsections.title: Power check
content: Sum of absorbed powers = 0 (sources deliver negative absorption). Use it to verify every DC solution in seconds.
Resistor power forms: $I^{2}R = V^{2}/R = VI$ - pick the known quantity.

quickRevision: Voltage divider: self on top. Current divider: opposite on top.
KCL nodes, KVL loops. Power sums to zero.
readingSections.companyNote: One divider + one KCL/KVL question is standard in prelims.

readingSections.title: 2. Network Theorems - Node/Mesh, Superposition, Thevenin/Norton, Max Power
readingSections.quickSummary: Node writes KCL at unknowns, mesh writes KVL in windows. Superposition kills all-but-one source. Thevenin compresses any linear network to Vth+Rth.
content: Nodal: pick reference (ground), assign node voltages, write KCL at each unknown node ($\sum$ leaving currents = 0, each $V_{diff}/R$), solve. Supernode when a voltage source bridges two unknown nodes. Mesh: assign clockwise mesh currents, write KVL per window ($R_{self}I_{m} - \sum R_{shared}I_{neighbour} = \sum$ rises), solve. Supermesh when a current source is shared by two meshes.

Superposition: linear circuits only - keep ONE independent source alive at a time (voltage shorted, current opened), solve, ADD results. Dependent sources stay on always. Power does NOT superpose (quadratic) - compute power last from total V/I.

Thevenin: any linear two-terminal network = $V_{th}$ (open-circuit voltage) in series with $R_{th}$. Norton: same as $I_{N}$ (short-circuit current) in parallel with $R_{N} = R_{th}$. Conversions: $V_{th} = I_{N}R_{th}$. $R_{th}$ = deactivate independents (short V, open I) and look back; with dependent sources use test-source ($1A/1V$) method.
Maximum power transfer: load gets most when $R_{L} = R_{th}$, and $P_{max} = V_{th}^{2}/(4R_{th})$. Efficiency then is only 50% - used for signals, never for power grids.

subsections.title: Thevenin in 3 steps
content: Step 1: remove load, find open-circuit voltage = $V_{th}$ (divider/node often enough).
Step 2: deactivate sources, find $R_{th}$ by series/parallel (or test source).
Step 3: reconnect load to $V_{th}$-$R_{th}$ and solve trivially.

example.prompt: 12V source, series 2k to node A, 4k from A to ground. Thevenin at A?

subsections.title: Superposition traps
content: Short voltage sources (0V) but never short a current source; open current sources but never open a voltage source.
Dependent sources never deactivated. Power needs totals first.
Two-source circuits split into two one-source halves - each half is usually a divider.

subsections.title: Max power line
content: Set $R_{L} = R_{th}$ first, then $P_{max} = V_{th}^{2}/4R_{th}$.
If $R_{L}$ is fixed and unequal, power is $V_{th}^{2}R_{L}/(R_{th}+R_{L})^{2}$ - less than max.

quickRevision: Node=KCL, mesh=KVL. Supernode/supermesh for bridging sources.
Superposition: one source alive, add (not power).
Thevenin Vth+Rth; Norton IN||RN; RL=Rth for max power.

readingSections.title: 3. RC Circuits - Transients, Impedance, RMS (VEDA Sample Heart)
readingSections.quickSummary: Capacitor blocks DC when charged, passes changes. tau=RC sets speed. Sine steady state uses complex impedance. RMS adds orthogonally in series RC.
content: Capacitor $Q = CV$, $I = C\,dV/dt$. DC steady state: open circuit (charged, no current). Charging toward source through $R$: $V_{C}(t) = V_{s}(1-e^{-t/\tau})$, $\tau = RC$. After $5\tau$ it is settled (>99%). Discharging: $V_{C} = V_{0}e^{-t/\tau}$.

Sine steady state at $\omega$: $Z_{R} = R$, $Z_{C} = 1/(j\omega C) = -j/(\omega C)$, $Z_{L} = j\omega L$. Series: add. Magnitude $|Z| = \sqrt{R^{2}+X^{2}}$, current $I = V/|Z|$, resistor and capacitor voltages are $90^{\circ}$ apart so they add by Pythagoras, NOT directly.
VEDA sample: series RC with $V_{R} = 12V$ RMS, $V_{C} = 15V$ RMS. Source $V_{s} = \sqrt{12^{2}+15^{2}} = \sqrt{369} \approx 19.2V$ RMS. Adding $12+15 = 27V$ is the classic trap.

Linear circuits never create new frequencies: $6kHz$ sine in gives $6kHz$ everywhere (only amplitude/phase change). So the voltage across the resistor in the $6kHz$ series-RC question is still $6kHz$.

Impedance design ($1+4j \, \Omega$ at $\omega = 1$): real part 1 = $1\Omega$ resistor; imaginary $+j4$ = inductor $j\omega L = j4$ so $L = 4H$. Simplest: $1\Omega$ in series with $4H$. (Capacitor gives $-j$; to use one you would add a bigger inductor and subtract - pointless.)

Square-wave + RC ($R=1k, C=1\mu F$, $200Hz$): $\tau = RC = 1ms$, period $T = 5ms$, half-period $2.5ms = 2.5\tau$ - transitional regime. Low-pass (C shunt): exponential charge/discharge edges, visible rounding/tilt, average preserved. High-pass (C series): tilted square with sag toward zero between edges. Rule of thumb: $T/2 \gg \tau$ passes shape; $T/2 \ll \tau$ differentiates/integrates into spikes/ramps.

subsections.title: tau intuition
content: $\tau = RC$: bigger $R$ (slow fill) or bigger $C$ (big tank) means slower.
$1\tau$: 63% there. $2.2\tau$: 90%. $5\tau$: settled.
VEDA's $1ms$ vs $2.5ms$ half-cycle sits mid-scale - expect clear exponentials, not corners.

subsections.title: RMS Pythagoras
content: Resistor voltage is in phase with current (real power); L/C voltages are quadrature (reactive).

subsections.title: Frequency preservation
content: R, L, C are linear: output frequencies equal input frequencies present.
New frequencies need nonlinearity (diodes - next section) or switching.
So $6kHz$ in, $6kHz$ out - amplitude/phase only.

quickRevision: tau=RC; 5tau settled. DC steady: C open.
Series RMS adds by Pythagoras, not directly.
Linear: frequency in = frequency out. 1+4j at w=1: 1 ohm + 4H.
readingSections.companyNote: All four VEDA circuit-basic samples live in this section - master tau, RMS, frequency, impedance.

readingSections.title: 4. PN Diode - Models, Rectifiers, Clipping, Clamping
readingSections.quickSummary: Diode conducts forward (0.7V Si), blocks reverse. Rectifiers turn AC to pulsating DC; clippers slice levels; clampers shift the whole waveform.
content: IV: forward exponential past knee (~0.7V Si, ~0.3V Ge), reverse tiny saturation current until breakdown. Exam models: ideal (0V drop, perfect switch), constant-drop (0.7V when on), piecewise-linear (+ small $r_{d}$). State assumption method: guess on/off, solve, check consistency (on needs forward bias, off needs reverse).

Half-wave rectifier: passes one half-cycle, blocks other. No filter: $V_{dc} = V_{p}/\pi$, ripple frequency = input $f$. Full-wave bridge: both halves used (4 diodes, no centre tap): $V_{dc} = 2V_{p}/\pi$, ripple $2f$, PIV per diode = $V_{p}$ (bridge) vs $2V_{p}$ (centre-tapped). Capacitor filter charges to $V_{p}$, sags between peaks: full-wave ripple $V_{r} \approx I_{DC}/(2fC)$, half-wave $I_{DC}/(fC)$. Bigger $C$ or lighter load smooths.

Clippers: diode (+reference $V_{ref}$) clips the top (shunt diode to $V_{ref}$) or bottom (reversed). Series clipper blocks one polarity entirely. Transfer curve ($V_{o}$ vs $V_{i}$) has slope $1$ (pass) and $0$ (clip) segments meeting at the reference (plus 0.7V if non-ideal).

Clampers: C + diode + $V_{ref}$ shift the DC level without changing shape: capacitor holds the peak difference, diode conducts briefly each cycle to restore it. Positive clamper pushes waveform up (negative peaks to $V_{ref}$); negative clamper pushes down. Rule: the peak touched by the diode is clamped to $V_{ref}$ (minus diode drop).

subsections.title: Rectifier numbers to memorise
content: Half-wave $V_{dc} = V_{p}/\pi \approx 0.318V_{p}$, ripple $f$.
Full-wave $V_{dc} = 2V_{p}/\pi \approx 0.636V_{p}$, ripple $2f$.
Capacitor filter: $V_{dc} \approx V_{p}$, ripple $I/(2fC)$ full-wave, $I/(fC)$ half-wave.

example.prompt: Bridge, 10V peak sine, no filter. Vdc?

subsections.title: Clipper sketch recipe
content: Find diode-on condition (anode > cathode + 0.7). Solve output in on-state (clipped level) and off-state (follower).
Join segments at the transition input. Ideal ($0V$) shifts levels by $0.7V$ vs practical - note the model.

subsections.title: Clamper sketch recipe
content: Assume steady state: capacitor holds $V_{C} = $ peak difference. Diode on only at one extreme per cycle.
Output = input $\pm V_{C}$ shifted so the touched peak sits at $V_{ref}$.
Shape and peak-to-peak never change - only DC level moves.

quickRevision: Half Vp/pi at f; full 2Vp/pi at 2f; cap filter to Vp.
readingSections.companyNote: Syllabus names clipping, clamping and rectifiers explicitly - one sketch each is typical.

readingSections.title: 5. Zener Diode and BJT Basics
readingSections.quickSummary: Zener holds reverse voltage constant for regulation. BJT: small base current controls large collector current; modes are cutoff/active/saturation.
content: Zener: heavily doped for sharp reverse breakdown at $V_{Z}$. Regulator: series resistor drops the excess, Zener holds load at $V_{Z}$ while $I_{Z}$ stays between knee ($I_{Zmin}$) and power limit ($I_{Zmax} = P_{Z}/V_{Z}$). Needs $V_{in} > V_{Z}$ plus headroom, and load current bounded so the Zener never starves ($I_{Z} = I_{R} - I_{L} > 0$).

BJT structure: NPN ($n$-$p$-$n$) and PNP (arrow on emitter shows conventional outflow for NPN... emitter arrow points out for NPN, in for PNP). Two junctions: base-emitter (controls) and base-collector. Active mode: BE forward ($V_{BE} \approx 0.7V$ NPN), BC reverse; $I_{C} = \beta I_{B}$, $I_{E} = I_{C}+I_{B} = (\beta+1)I_{B}$.

Modes: cutoff (both reverse: OFF, $I_{C} \approx 0$) - digital 0/standby. Active (BE fwd, BC rev: amplifier, $I_{C} = \beta I_{B}$) - analog gain. Saturation (both forward: ON switch, $V_{CE,sat} \approx 0.2V$, $I_{C} < \beta I_{B}$) - digital 1 pull. Inverted (swapped, low gain) - avoid. VEDA depth stops at modes + switch reading + simple bias currents unless the poster adds more.

Digital view: BJT as switch - cutoff = open, saturation = closed ($0.2V$). That plus diode AND/OR thinking covers most VEDA BJT questions; small-signal ($g_{m}, r_{\pi}$) belongs to the analog paper, not this one.

subsections.title: Zener current window
content: Series current $I_{R} = (V_{in}-V_{Z})/R$. Load takes $I_{L} = V_{Z}/R_{L}$. Zener keeps $I_{Z} = I_{R}-I_{L}$.
Regulation holds while $I_{Zmin} < I_{Z} < I_{Zmax}$ across line/load corners.
Design picks $R$ for worst case (min $V_{in}$, max $I_{L}$ still leaves $I_{Zmin}$).

subsections.title: BJT mode table
content: Cutoff: BE rev, BC rev - OFF.
Active: BE fwd, BC rev - $I_{C}=\beta I_{B}$.
Saturation: BE fwd, BC fwd - switch ON ($V_{CE} \approx 0.2V$).
Test order: assume active, check $V_{CE} > V_{CE,sat}$ (NPN); else saturated.

subsections.title: NPN vs PNP currents
content: NPN: conventional currents flow in ($I_{B},I_{C}$ into device for active biasing with positive rails).
PNP: mirror image - emitter to higher voltage, currents flow out. Arrow direction is the emitter-current direction.

quickRevision: Zener: Vz held while Iz in window; R drops the rest.
Active Ic=B Ib; saturation VCE 0.2V switch; cutoff off.
readingSections.companyNote: BJT depth here is modes + switch + bias currents; small-signal is the analog-domain paper.

readingSections.title: 6. Exam Waveform Skills - Sketching Vout Under Time Pressure
readingSections.quickSummary: Compare half-period with tau, use RMS Pythagoras for sine, keep frequency, clamp touches one peak.
content: RC + square wave drill: (1) compute $\tau = RC$ and $T/2$; (2) ratio $T/2\tau$ decides: $>5$ square-ish, $<0.2$ spikes/ramps, in-between exponential tilt (VEDA's $2.5$); (3) mark start levels from previous half-cycle continuity (capacitor voltage cannot jump); (4) draw exponentials toward asymptotes ($V_{s}$ for charge, $0$/opposite for discharge).

Diode + sine drill: (1) mark diode-on intervals (anode > cathode); (2) draw conducting levels (0V ideal / 0.7V / $V_{ref}$); (3) draw blocked intervals as follower (clipper) or shifted copy (clamper); (4) label peaks and zero crossings.
RMS drill: identify series quadrature pair first ($R$ vs $X$), then Pythagoras; never add magnitudes linearly. Frequency drill: linear R/C network - output has input's frequencies only.

Presentation: axes labelled ($V,t$ with units), $\tau$ and $T/2$ marked, peak values written, diode states annotated per interval. Examiners award method marks for these labels even if a segment wobbles.

subsections.title: Continuity rules
content: Capacitor voltage cannot jump (needs infinite current). Inductor current cannot jump (needs infinite voltage).
Use the end of one interval as the start of the next - the whole sketch chains.
Resistor voltage/current CAN jump - fine.

subsections.title: Asymptote habit
content: Charging aims at source level; discharging aims at zero (or opposite source).
Draw the faint asymptote first, then the exponential approaching it - looks professional and stays accurate.

subsections.title: Model statement
content: Write Ideal (0V) or Si (0.7V) at the top. Level answers shift by exactly the drop.
If unspecified, solve ideal first, then note the 0.7V shift - covers both markings.

quickRevision: tau vs T/2 sets the shape regime.
C voltage continuous; R can jump.
readingSections.companyNote: The 4-mark waveform question rewards labelled method - never submit a bare curve.
